newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian income to quadruple in 25 yrs - Chidambaram.
newsitem.headline: Indian income to quadruple in 25 yrs - Chidambaram.

text.p: Indian Finance Minister P. Chidambaram said on Wednesday that the nation's per capita income would quadruple over the next 25 years, allowing the second most populous nation to eradicate poverty.
"The per capita income will be raised by four times in 25 years, by which India will have abolished poverty," Chidambaram told a business conference.
In the 1995/96 (April-March) financial year, per capita income was 2,897 rupees, up from 2,777 in 1994/95, according to government estimates.

The figures were based on population estimates of 904 million in 1994/95 and 920 million in 1995/96. Private sector population experts say India currently has more than 930 million people, ranking it behind China in population.
Chidambaram said growth of gross domestic product (GDP), which touched 7.0 percent in 1996/97 (April-March), was not strong enough.
"Even that is not enough. We are aiming at eight percent by the turn of the century," Chidambaram said.
He said India averaged GDP growth of 5.5 percent in the 1980s but over the next few years it should average 7.5 percent a year.
"The difference between 7.5 and 5.5 percent appears to be small but in a country with 950 million people it means doubling of per capita income," Chidambaram said.
